correctness.rationale: The source threshold is rewritten exactly with \(r=(\varsigma+1)^{-1}\). Strict mass monotonicity follows from a positive derivative whose numerator has an explicitly positive derivative; particle-number monotonicity is immediate from the unique \(N\)-dependent term. Endpoint limits yield the exact finite-\(N\) feasibility inequality. The all-\(N\) criterion uses a monotone limit that is never attained at finite \(N\), explaining the non-strict \(\gamma\ge G\) condition. The two square-root laws follow from the displayed small-\(r\) expansions after first proving \(r\to0\). No finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source emphasizes uniform boundedness of its threshold but does not resolve how the theorem behaves when particle number and mass are quantified in different orders. The new classification identifies the natural critical strength \\(2/\\pi\\) separating finite-size certification from one-mass certification for arbitrarily large finite \(N\), gives the exact finite-\(N\) ceiling below that value, and quantifies the critical mass growth on both sides. These are structural many-body consequences of the stability certificate rather than an arbitrary parameter substitution.
